sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
Deeds for New Hanover County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds in downtown Wilmington, at 320 Chestnut Street, Suite 102. The county tells filers to send every mailed recording to that Suite 102 address and nowhere else.

New Hanover County Register of Deeds locations, as listed on the county's Register of Deeds page

sections.h2: What does New Hanover County require on the front page of a deed?
sections.html:
The county asks for more than the bare statute. Each deed and deed of trust must show the drafter's name on its front page, and every document that conveys land must carry the tax ID number and the grantee's address there too.

Every document also needs the name and address of the person who should get the original back. A tax ID number comes from the Land Records section of the county Tax Department, reachable at 910-798-7300, so a seller or closing attorney can look it up before the deed is typed. Gather these items before the deed is typed so the front page is complete.

sections.h2: What paper standards apply to a New Hanover County recording?
sections.html:
A paper instrument has to meet the county's list or pay a $25.00 nonstandard fee under G.S. 161-10(a)(19), on top of the normal recording fees. The county lists these requirements:

  • Paper of 8 1/2 by 11 inches or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • A blank margin of three inches at the top of page one and one-half inch on the other sides, and on all sides of later pages.
  • Black print on white paper in a legible font, with 9 points treated as the smallest legible size.
  • Printing on one side of the page only.
  • The type of instrument stated at the top of page one, outside the blank margin.

Blanks may be completed in pen, and corrections may be made in black ink only. Cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages, in all forms, and UCC filings are exempt from these standards.

sections.h2: How much is the deed excise tax in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
The county prints the excise rate on its Register of Deeds page as $1.00 per $500.00 of the purchase price, which it describes as $2.00 per $1,000.00. State law makes the grantor, the seller, responsible for it.

G.S. 105-228.30 requires payment to the register before the deed goes on record, and it splits the money between the county general fund and the State. The register cannot tell a caller what a neighbor's house sold for, because the office can only give the amount of the excise stamp that was placed on the deed when it was recorded.

Recording fees, in contrast, come from the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10. That schedule charges no fee to record a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust, and it charges $64.00 for the first 35 pages of a deed of trust or mortgage.

sections.h2: What can the Register of Deeds do for a seller, and what can it not do?
sections.html:
It records documents, keeps them as public records and issues copies. It does not give legal advice, run title searches or send people to attorneys. The county's FAQ is direct about the limits.

  • All records except DD-214 military discharges are public, and anyone may view or copy them in the office.
  • The office does not tell you whether a lien has been removed. You need an attorney or title company for that.
  • To remove or add a name on a deed you need a new deed drawn up and filed.
  • Wills are filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, in the Estate division, not with the Register of Deeds.
  • The office holds subdivision and condominium plats, not individual property surveys.
  • The house's age and square footage come from the Tax Department.

The register also offers a free fraud alert. If a document is recorded in your name, you get an email with a copy at no cost, a useful protection for an owner of a vacant or inherited house.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows registration time. A buyer in New Hanover County gets that protection only when the deed reaches the Wilmington office.

The rule applies to a cash sale just as it does to a financed one. Because the office does not search titles, ask an attorney or title company to check for open liens before the deed is signed.

sections.h2: What do New Hanover County housing figures say about local sellers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 245,959 people lived in New Hanover County on July 1, 2025, in 128,402 housing units. The owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024 was 61.4%, which leaves about 39% of occupied homes as rentals, and median gross rent was $1,417.

Only 83.8% of residents had lived in the same house a year earlier, and the county issued 2,332 building permits in 2025. Households numbered 104,856 for 2020 to 2024, at 2.19 people each, and 45.4% of adults 25 and older held a bachelor's degree or higher. For a seller, the practical lesson from the county's rules is simple: bring a deed with the drafter's name, the tax ID and the grantee address on page one.

sections.h2: What other services does the New Hanover County office run?
sections.html:
Beyond land records, the Wilmington office handles vital records, certified copies of births, deaths and marriage licenses, passport services, military discharge filings and e-filing of assumed business name certificates. Marriage licenses are by appointment only, while notary oaths need no appointment.

The county's page also links a public records search and a guide titled "Don't Overpay for a Copy of Your House Deed." Sellers who need a copy of their own deed for a closing can start there before ordering a paid copy. Owners of rental houses who operate under a business name can use the e-filing link for that certificate, and the Register of Deeds courtesy forms for business names are printed from the Secretary of State's website.

faqs.q: Where is the New Hanover County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The main office is at 320 Chestnut Street in Wilmington, with real estate recording in Suite 102. A satellite office at 230 Government Center Drive takes recordings from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the New Hanover County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, but mail it only to 320 Chestnut Street, Suite 102, Wilmington, NC 28401. The county says not to mail recordings to the satellite office.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax on a New Hanover County deed?
faqs.a: The county prints it as $1.00 per $500.00 of the purchase price, or $2.00 per $1,000.00, and the seller pays it. The register can only report the stamp amount shown on a recorded deed.

faqs.q: Where do I get the tax ID number for a New Hanover County deed?
faqs.a: Call the Land Records section of the county Tax Department at 910-798-7300. The tax ID must appear on the front page of any document that conveys land, along with the grantee's address.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds file wills in New Hanover County?
faqs.a: No. Wills are filed in the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court. The Register of Deeds records the deeds that pass title afterward.
